newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Net profits of S.Korea foreign bank branches rise.
newsitem.headline: Net profits of S.Korea foreign bank branches rise.

text.p: Foreign bank branches in South Korea recorded a combined 169.7 billion won of net profits in the first half of their respective fiscal years, up 39.2 percent from a year earlier, the Bank of Korea (BOK) said on Tuesday.
A BOK official said 32 of the 37 foreign bank branches in the country close books at the end of December, two at the end of September and three others at the end of October.
A BOK report attributed the brisk net profit growth to increased income from operations of foreign currency-denominated assets, investment in derivatives and foreign exchange trading.
Their interest income from foreign currency-denominated assets rose 36 percent year-on-year and income from foreign exchange trading increased 177.3 percent, the report said.
Chase Manhattan Bank posted the biggest half-year net profit of 37.15 billion won, followed by Citibank with 11.96 billion won profit and Credit Lyonnais with 10.48 billion.
The First National Bank of Boston topped the list in terms of return on assets by recording 6.04 percent, followed by Chase Manhattan with 4.94 percent.
